title: Complete-intersection neighbourhoods detected by the completed local ring
statement: Let $k$ be a field, $S$ a finitely generated $k$-algebra [def-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra], $\mathfrak p\subset S$ a maximal ideal, $A=S_{\mathfrak p}$ [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime], and $F=S/\mathfrak p$. Let $\widehat A$ be the completion at the maximal ideal [def-weil-pbc-adic-completion]. The following are equivalent: (1) some principal affine neighbourhood of $\mathfrak p$, $\operatorname{Spec}S_g$ with $g\notin\mathfrak p$ [def-weil-ring-localization-away, def-weil-affine-spectrum], has coordinate algebra a local complete intersection over $k$ [def-weil-pbc-complete-intersection-over-field]; (2) for some integers $r,c\ge0$, $\widehat A$ is isomorphic as a ring to $F[[z_1,\ldots,z_r]]/(h_1,\ldots,h_c)$, where $h_1,\ldots,h_c$ is a regular sequence in the maximal ideal $(z_1,\ldots,z_r)$ [def-weil-pbc-multivariate-power-series, def-weil-pbc-regular-sequence]. When these equivalent conditions hold, $\operatorname{depth}(A)=\dim A$ [def-weil-pbc-depth, def-weil-pbc-krull-dimension-ring]. In particular, if $S$ itself is a local complete intersection over $k$, then this depth equality holds at every maximal ideal.

source.place: Tags 09Q1 (lemma-quotient-regular-ring), 09Q3 (definition-lci) and 09Q6 (lemma-check-lci-agrees), combined with Algebra Tags 00SG (lemma-lci-at-prime) and 00SB (lemma-lci-CM).

proof.text: Choose a surjection $P=k[x_1,\ldots,x_n]\to S$ from [def-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra], with kernel $I$, and let $\mathfrak q$ be the inverse image of $\mathfrak p$. By [lem-weil-pbc-polynomial-ring-field-regular-ring], $R=P_{\mathfrak q}$ is regular local and hence Noetherian. The map $R/IR\to A$, $(u/v)\bmod IR\mapsto\bar u/\bar v$, is an isomorphism: both sides invert exactly the images of $P\setminus\mathfrak q$ in $P/I$, and their kernels are the fractions with numerator in $I$. Thus [lem-weil-pbc-surjective-image-noetherian] makes $A$ Noetherian. Put $C=\widehat A$. By [lem-weil-pbc-adic-completion-noetherian] and [lem-weil-pbc-local-completion-local-ring], $C$ is Noetherian local with maximal ideal $\mathfrak n=\mathfrak pAC$ and residue field $F$. By [lem-weil-pbc-adic-completion-mod-ideal], it is $\mathfrak n$-adically complete.

source.place: 09Q6 (lemma-check-lci-agrees), proof of (1): polynomial-local presentation; Algebra 0316, 05GI and 05GG for the completion.

proof.text: The structural maps make $C$ contain the field $k$: a unital map from a field into a nonzero local ring is injective. In particular $C$ and its residue field $F$ have the same characteristic. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-cohen-coefficient-ring-exists] to $C$. Its coefficient subring $\Lambda$ has maximal ideal $p\Lambda$, where $p$ is the characteristic of $F$. This ideal is zero: for $p=0$ by definition, and for $p>0$ because $pC=0$ and $\Lambda\subseteq C$. Hence $\Lambda$ is a field, since each nonzero element lies outside its zero maximal ideal and is a unit. The coefficient-ring residue isomorphism therefore gives a ring map $\alpha:F\to C$ whose composite with $C\to F$ is the identity. This choice need not respect the originally given embedding of $k$; the required conclusion is an isomorphism of rings.

source.place: 032A (theorem-cohen-structure-theorem), part (1), and 0326 (definition-coefficient-ring), remark case (1): a coefficient ring in a complete local ring containing a field is a coefficient field.

proof.text: Choose generators $y_1,\ldots,y_r$ of $\mathfrak n$, possible since $C$ is Noetherian [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring]. Set $Q=F[[z_1,\ldots,z_r]]$. By [lem-weil-pbc-power-series-field-cohen-regular-complete], $Q$ is complete regular local with maximal ideal $\mathfrak l=(z_1,\ldots,z_r)$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-power-series-universal-property-complete] to $C,\mathfrak n,\alpha,(y_i)$ to obtain $\psi:Q\to C$, $z_i\mapsto y_i$. The extended ideal $\mathfrak lC$ is exactly $\mathfrak n$. The source is $\mathfrak l$-adically complete, the target is $\mathfrak n$-adically Hausdorff, and $Q\to C/\mathfrak n=F$ is surjective because constants map through the residue section $\alpha$. Therefore [lem-weil-pbc-complete-source-surjective-mod-ideal] makes $\psi$ surjective. Its kernel lies in $\mathfrak l$: a series outside $\mathfrak l$ is a unit, whose image cannot vanish in the nonzero ring $C$.

Assume (1). By the covering in [def-weil-pbc-complete-intersection-over-field], the prime of $S_g$ induced by $\mathfrak p$ belongs to some $D(a)$ with $T=(S_g)_a$ a global complete intersection. This ring is nonzero because it has that prime. Unpack its presentation $T\cong k[w_1,\ldots,w_m]/(f_1,\ldots,f_t)$ with $\dim T=m-t$. Let $\mathfrak q_T$ be the prime of the polynomial ring corresponding to our point and $R_T=k[w_1,\ldots,w_m]_{\mathfrak q_T}$. By [lem-weil-pbc-polynomial-ring-field-regular-ring], $R_T$ is regular local, and [lem-weil-pbc-global-complete-intersection-local-regular-sequence] says the images of the $f_i$ form a regular sequence there. The fractions identify $A\cong R_T/(f_1,\ldots,f_t)$: the elements inverted in passing from $S$ to $T$ were already outside $\mathfrak p$. Apply [lem-trf-regular-quotient-completion-kernel-test] to this regular-local quotient and the regular-local surjection $\psi:Q\to C$ of step 3. It makes $\ker\psi$ generated by a regular sequence $h_1,\ldots,h_c$ in $\mathfrak l$. The quotient map induces the ring isomorphism $Q/(h_1,\ldots,h_c)\cong C$, proving (2).

source.place: 09Q0 (lemma-quotient-regular-ring-by-regular-sequence) and 09Q1 (lemma-quotient-regular-ring), with 09PZ; Algebra 00SB proof for regularity of the equations in a global complete intersection.

proof.text: Conversely assume (2). The ring $Q_0=F[[z_1,\ldots,z_r]]$ in that condition is regular local by [lem-weil-pbc-power-series-field-cohen-regular-complete]. Composing its quotient map with the stated ring isomorphism gives a surjection $Q_0\to C$ whose kernel is generated by the given regular sequence $(h_1,\ldots,h_c)$. Apply [lem-trf-regular-quotient-completion-kernel-test] to $R=P_{\mathfrak q}$ and $IR$ from step 1 and this surjection. It gives a regular sequence generating $IR$. By [lem-weil-pbc-lci-regular-sequence-global-complete-intersection], applied to the presentation $P/I\cong S$ at $\mathfrak p$, there is $g\notin\mathfrak p$ with $S_g$ a global complete intersection. It is a local complete intersection by [def-weil-pbc-complete-intersection-over-field], using the single open $D(1)$ as cover. This proves (1).

source.place: 09Q1 (lemma-quotient-regular-ring), (1) implies (2), and Algebra 00SC (lemma-lci), (5) implies (1); this is the local-to-neighbourhood passage of 00SG (lemma-lci-at-prime).

proof.text: Under these equivalent conditions use the regular-local quotient $A\cong R_T/(f_1,\ldots,f_t)$ from step 4. Its regular ambient ring has finite dimension $d$ by [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-local-finite-krull-dimension]. By [def-weil-regular-scheme], choose $d$ generators of its maximal ideal; [lem-weil-pbc-regular-local-generators-regular-sequence] makes them a regular sequence, so [def-weil-pbc-depth] gives $\operatorname{depth}R_T\ge d$. Put $R_i=R_T/(f_1,\ldots,f_i)$ for $0\le i\le t$. Inductively $R_i$ is Noetherian local and $\operatorname{depth}R_i\ge\dim R_i$: the base is the preceding inequality; at index $i<t$, regularity of $(f_j)$ says $f_{i+1}$ is a nonzerodivisor on $R_i$, and its image lies in the maximal ideal. Thus [lem-weil-pbc-cm-local-quotient-nonzerodivisor-cm] gives exactly the induction assertion for $R_{i+1}$. All quotients are nonzero because the equations lie in the maximal ideal. In particular $\operatorname{depth}A\ge\dim A$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-depth-le-support-dimension] to the nonzero finite $A$-module $A$ to obtain the reverse inequality: its support is all of $\operatorname{Spec}A$, since $1/1=0$ in $A_{\mathfrak r}$ would force an element outside $\mathfrak r$ to equal zero. Therefore $\operatorname{depth}A=\dim A$. If $S$ itself is a local complete intersection, condition (1) holds at every maximal ideal with $g=1$, proving the last sentence.

lean.statement: theorem completion_local_complete_intersection_iff (k : Type u) (S : Type v) [Field k] [CommRing S] [Algebra k S] [Algebra.FiniteType k S] (p : Ideal S) [p.IsMaximal] : ((∃ g : S, g ∉ p ∧ IsLocalCompleteIntersection k (Localization.Away g)) ↔ (∃ (r c : ℕ) (h : Fin c → MvPowerSeries (Fin r) (S ⧸ p)), RingTheory.Sequence.IsRegular (MvPowerSeries (Fin r) (S ⧸ p)) (List.ofFn h) ∧ (∀ i : Fin c, h i ∈ Ideal.span (Set.range (fun j : Fin r => MvPowerSeries.X j))) ∧ Nonempty ((MvPowerSeries (Fin r) (S ⧸ p) ⧸ Ideal.span (Set.range h)) ≃+* AdicCompletion (IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal (Localization.AtPrime p)) (Localization.AtPrime p)))) ∧ ((∃ g : S, g ∉ p ∧ IsLocalCompleteIntersection k (Localization.Away g)) → (↑(IsLocalRing.depth (R := Localization.AtPrime p) (Localization.AtPrime p)) : WithBot ℕ∞) = ringKrullDim (Localization.AtPrime p)) ∧ (IsLocalCompleteIntersection k S → ∀ (q : Ideal S) [hq : q.IsMaximal], (↑(IsLocalRing.depth (R := Localization.AtPrime q) (Localization.AtPrime q)) : WithBot ℕ∞) = ringKrullDim (Localization.AtPrime q))
